extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes a robust testing framework for predictive regressions with lagged autoregressive variables that is resistant to anomalous observations (outliers). The method utilizes a robust Huber M-estimator (weighted least squares with data-driven weights) to bound the influence of outliers. To perform inference, the authors develop a fast resampling (bootstrap and subsampling) approach that avoids the high computational cost of repeatedly solving robust estimation equations on simulated samples.
extraction.universe: S&P 500 index and value-weighted CRSP index (including NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ stocks)

key_findings: Conventional predictability tests (bias-corrected, local-to-unity, standard bootstrap/subsampling) are highly nonresistant to small fractions of anomalous observations, which drastically reduces their power to detect predictability.
The proposed robust fast resampling framework maintains high power and correct size in the presence of outliers, while keeping computational costs sustainable.

Empirical analysis shows that the dividend yield is a robust predictor of US market returns across all subperiods, frequencies, and horizons, whereas conventional tests fail to reject the null of no predictability in several subperiods (e.g., 1995-2010).
The variance risk premium is confirmed as a robust predictor of future market returns at quarterly horizons under both robust and nonrobust testing methods.

Anomalous observations (less than 5% of the data, clustering during the NASDAQ bubble and 2008 financial crisis) are responsible for the failure of conventional testing methods in uncovering hidden predictability.
limitations: The robust subsampling tests require symmetric confidence intervals to ensure correct asymptotic size uniformly in the degree of persistence, as lower and equal-tailed conventional subsampling intervals have incorrect size asymptotically.
The robust approach does not improve quarterly out-of-sample forecasts over the standard sample mean for the Santos and Veronesi model (R2_OS,ROB is negative).
The paper focuses on standard predictive systems with autocorrelated regressors, leaving potential extensions to nonlinear predictive relations or unobserved state variables for future research.
